newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli minister asks EU to ease rules of origin.
newsitem.headline: Israeli minister asks EU to ease rules of origin.

text.p: Israel Industry and Trade Minister Natan Sharansky has asked the European Union to grant Israel the same status as East European countries relating to rules of origin, the ministry said on Tuesday.

In a meeting on Monday with Jean Paul Jesse, the EU's head of delegation to Israel, Sharansky said the two sides needed to find ways to narrow Israel's chronic trade deficit with the EU, which he said reached about $10 billion last year.
Sharansky said he was seeking measures to open EU markets to Israeli exports rather than simply identifying and eliminating the EU's non-tariff barriers.
He said easing the rules of origin would enable products containing Israeli-made parts and components to be traded more freely between East and West Europe.

Sharansky also proposed that the EU ease rules of origin for products made jointly by Israel and other Middle Eastern countries. He added that such a move would aid the peace process by encouraging regional economic development.
Israel and the EU have a free trade agreement.
The ministry quoted Jesse as saying the EU could not extend free trade benefits to the region so long as there was no free trade in the Middle East itself.
